title: Preference data and Bradley-Terry reward models
outcome: Derive a pairwise reward likelihood, test its invariances and identify what comparison data cannot determine.

exercises.title: Equal scores
exercises.task: Evaluate a positive comparison when both scores are zero.
exercises.hint: Use the logistic link and softplus form.
exercises.answer: Equal scores express no preference under the model; observing a chosen response still incurs positive negative log likelihood.

exercises.title: Shift both rewards
exercises.expected: Loss and score gradient remain unchanged.
exercises.answer: Pairwise labels cannot determine a common reward offset, including prompt-specific offsets when comparisons stay within prompts.

exercises.title: Reverse empirical counts
exercises.task: Use one win and three losses.
exercises.answer: Reversing labels changes the sign of the fitted log odds, while finite counts still imply uncertainty.

exercises.title: All wins and no losses
exercises.task: Fit an unregularized pair with four wins and zero losses.
exercises.hint: Log odds diverge at a boundary probability.
exercises.answer: Regularization or a prior can produce a finite estimate, but it changes the model and must be stated.

exercises.title: Test numerical stability
exercises.task: Use scores-1000 and 1000 for the preferred/rejected pair.
exercises.answer: Stable softplus arithmetic preserves the large finite loss without underflowing a probability to zero first.

exercises.title: Interpret a preference cycle
exercises.task: Observe A>B, B>C and C>A across labels.
exercises.expected: A deterministic scalar ordering cannot satisfy all three.
exercises.hint: Add the three proposed positive score differences.
exercises.answer: Their sum would need to be positive while algebraically equaling zero. Investigate stochasticity, annotator heterogeneity and multiple criteria.
